title: What is the best way to generate 2d assets and animate characters?
author: oaishere
selftext:
Hey, I want to build an action 2d game, (hades is a good example of how i'd want it to look like)  
what is the actual standard way of doing this?  
no matter how i build the game, phaser/godot - 2 different engines, im always stuck on bad visuals, I know Astra makes it way better but its still not good enough to get good visuals, both for effects and for character animations, maybe AI is just not at this level yet and i should stick to different type of games ?

comments.author: lyeeedar
comments.body:
Start with a model like illustrious or anima or krea with a set of Loras to get the look you want. Then animate it with minimax or wan2.2 using image to video. To make this look better you can also generate the end frame with an edit model like Qwen image edit, Gemini 3.1 flash lite image, or gpt image 2, then do first frame last frame. Take the video and decompose it to frames, there's your sprite sheet.

You will need to experiment with prompts, framing, and repair. Some hand cleanup may be required.

comments.author: CS_Asset_Factory
comments.body:
The thing that broke this for us wasn't image quality, it was identity across images. A game needs the same character many times: eight frames of a walk, four facings, then again holding a different weapon. General image models optimise each picture on its own, so you end up with four lovely sprites of four slightly different people.

Two things helped. For characters we moved to a model built specifically for pixel art, with rotation and animation endpoints, because holding identity across a frame set is what it is actually trained for. For tiles we stopped generating images at all and generate them in code, because a tile has to line up exactly and a model that is 99 percent right still leaves a visible seam.

The honest limit: we shipped one pack whose west facing frames are a mirror of east, because the generated west came back malformed.

comments.author: Nasilbitatbirakti
comments.body: Difficultiy depends on several things but I wouldn't do isometric 2D. Not only you need consistency within single animation but you need consistency among different animations from many different angles. AI just sucks at that. It's better to go 3D at that point. If you wanna do side scroller then it gets easier. But frame by frame spritesheets are still inconsistent and take up a lot of memory. You should do shaders and rigging whenever you can and use spritesheets only when you have to.

comments.author: RsetX
comments.body:
You could try my tool Sprite Sheep, it is a wrapper. It inject a workflow in Comfyui and download the video generation model as Minimax H3. You can download it from here: https://shaddafare.itch.io/sprite-sheep
Feedbacks are appreciated 👍🏻

comments.author: Entropydemic
comments.body: I sort of cheat my way around it. I make a video on Gemini and then cut it into a sprite sheet.

replies.author: schmitty812
replies.body: I did a similar thing with spriteflow. The videos just capture the animation so much better

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body:
Well, Hades created 3d models with hand drawn textures in a distinct 2d illustrative style. It then proceed to create sprite sheets with those models after animating them in 3d and positioning the camera at a locked angle. The environment, however, is a handpainted, isometric 2d.

Isometric is one of the hardest styles to do, whether AI or not, which is why studios have to go to these workarounds to actually get consistent visuals. It's a lot of extra work. And AI isn't really capable imo of producing quality visuals \*on its own\* yet. It can do a lot, but if you're not there to help walk it through the polish then it's only going to look good from curated trailers that carefully avoid showcasing all the little issues.

comments.author: unfamily_friendly
comments.body:
For 2D there's multiple approaches

Have money? Use GPT. It's really good

Have big GPU at least 8 gb? Use comfy UI with local model. Tho make sure it hase proper licensing. I sit on Klein

Wanna big control? Use Krita AI diffusion. This lets you not only make pictures, but also edit it piece by piece. Tbh best approach, but laborious

comments.author: ItsAlwaysTerminal
comments.body: You should specify Hades I or Hades 2. Hades 2 actually uses 3D models that are then converted.

comments.author: Careless-Cloud2009
comments.body:
I've tried comfyui, invoke ai and few other software specific tools with local ai. But mainly sd1.5 family. With multiple models and lora. 
My experience is not good for pixel art, looks bad and fails in consistency.
